doc.title: Ametria Dock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 4, 2019

title: Being sampled in the digital age and finding out when things go viral
summary: Rowe asks if she would learn of being sampled; Dock says yes, since anything popular spreads quickly on social media.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: That’s great. Speaking of the digital world, if someone like a rap artist or a rap producer sampled you and used you in a production, do you think you’d find out about it the way things work these days?

Sampled me, a vocal, like a riff or a run or something. Would I find out about it? Probably yes. And I’d find out if it went viral. And so that’s the thing about today, everything goes viral fast if it’s something that people like. And so yes, I think I would find out about it, and social media, I mean it would hit YouTube and Instagram, FaceBook, so fast that you know, I would know.
But this, I think it’s a good thing being taken advantage of in that way.
